## Personality

Jane Andrews is a steady, sensible, and lady-like individual known for her unflappable nerves and practical mindset. She plans to devote her entire life to teaching rather than marrying, drawn by the prospect of earning a salary.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. ## History

Jane Andrews attended Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) alongside [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Ruby Gillis](../character/ruby-gillis.md), earning a spot on the School Inspector's roll of honor. On the final day of school before graduation, she was so overwhelmed by emotion that she had to borrow a handkerchief from her brother. After completing her studies, she taught at [Newbridge](../codex/places.md#newbridge) school, earning the affection of the community, which was deeply distressed when she eventually left. Jane joined [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md) on a carriage ride to a charity concert at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel), where she later enjoyed a celebratory supper with her companions. While attending Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy), she frequently visited [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in town alongside [Josie Pye](../character/josie-pye.md) and Ruby. Later in her teaching career, Jane debated the ethics of corporal punishment with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) on the eve of a new school year. During a spring outing, she explored the woods and Hester Gray's forgotten garden with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md), though she found Anne's poetic ideas about nature difficult to grasp. Jane also served on a committee for the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers) alongside [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), successfully attempting to dissuade [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) from selling his fence space for painted advertising.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P4](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0004), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P28](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0028), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P33](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0033), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P34](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0034), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P38](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0038), +26 more_

## Quotes

> “Of course it would be romantic,” conceded Jane Andrews, “but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)

> “I don’t know how you’re going to prevent him,” exclaimed Jane bitterly. “Everybody knows what Judson Parker is. He’d do anything for money. He hasn’t a spark of public spirit or any sense of the beautiful.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P41](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0041)

> "Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)

> “Oh, Anne,” gasped Jane, as they fled to the girls’ dressing room amid hearty cheers. “Oh, Anne I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)

> "I’ll whip my pupils when they’re naughty. It’s the shortest and easiest way of convincing them."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 IV Different Opinions P14](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0014)
